notes:
CIRCUIT: a 5-column / 6-row ladder grid. The right-hand vertical rail carries five sources in series between the top rail and the bottom rail: V-AC 3V/1kHz (#0), I-AC 5A/1kHz (#2), V-DC 5V (#5), I-DC 10A (#8), V-DC 15V (#11). Four horizontal rungs (y~272, ~435, ~610, ~765) tap the right rail between consecutive sources and run left to an internal column. Four internal columns (A x~172, B x~305, C x~452, D x~625) hang from the top rail and run down to the bottom rail, carrying the L/C pairs.

NET MAP
  n1 = top rail y~115 plus the upper part of every internal column: 0.0 (V-AC top), 1.0 (1uH top, col A), 3.0 (5uH top, col B), 7.0 (10uH top, col C), 9.0 (50uH top, col D - col D gets there by hopping rungs 272/435/610).
  n2 = rung y~272 (node between V-AC and I-AC) + col A between the 1uH and the 5uF: 0.1, 2.0 (I-AC top), 1.1, 4.0 (5uF top).
  n3 = rung y~435 (node between I-AC and the 5V source) + col B between the 5uH and the 10uF: 2.1, 5.0, 3.1, 6.0.
  n4 = rung y~610 (node between the 5V source and the 10A source) AND rung y~765 (node between the 10A source and the 15V source) AND the bottom rail left of x~535. One net because col B carries the y~610 tap on down to the bottom rail (S36 + S55) and col C carries the y~765 tap on down to the same bottom rail (S52 + S56). Terminals: 5.1, 6.1 (10uF bottom), 8.0, 8.1 (I-DC both), 11.0 (15V top), 10.1 (50uF bottom), 4.1 (5uF bottom).
  n5 = col C between the 10uH and the 50uF: 7.1, 10.0.
  n6 = col D between the 50uH and the 100uF: 9.1, 12.0.
  n7 = bottom rail right of x~610 plus the bottom-right corner up to the 15V source: 12.1 (100uF bottom), 11.1 (15V bottom).

JUDGEMENT CALLS
  S11 (620,275), rung272 x col D. Tracer scored hop=0.0 dot=1.1 and defaulted to junction, but the 5x crop shows an unmistakable semicircular hop drawn on the column: OVERRIDDEN to crossing. Reading it as a junction would wire the top rail straight to the node below V-AC, i.e. short-circuit the 3V AC source - impossible, so crossing is forced on ink and on physics.
  S37 (606,612), rung610 x col D. Same case: hop metric only 1.3, defaulted to junction, but the crop shows the same left-bulging semicircle this drafter uses everywhere else (compare S22, S23, S38, S51). OVERRIDDEN to crossing. As a junction it would tie the top rail to the node between the 5V source and the 10A source and collapse n1 into n4.
  S34 / S38 + gap bridge B18 at (450,595)/(426,613): col C hopping rung610. The arc is clear, but the drafter's column stroke overshoots ~10px past the top of the arc and stops 5px short of the rung - inkmap at (451,610) shows ink at x=450-453 for y=598-607, blank rows 608-611, rung at y=612-615. The tracer bridged that 8px gap (B18) and thereby turned the hop into a junction, which shorted inductor #7 end to end. B18 DROPPED; S38 stays crossing, S34 stays junction (it only ties the column stub to the arc).
  S51 (604,763), rung765 x col D: crop shows the hop, kept as crossing.
  S52 (454,766) and S56 (452,902): both are clean T's at 10x - the rung ends on col C, col C ends on the bottom rail. Junctions, no ambiguity.
  S0/S1/S2 (top rail), S12/S24/S36 (rung left ends), S9/S21/S35/S50 (rung right ends) and S55: all plain T's -> junction.
  S10, S13, S22, S23: drawn hops -> crossing (agrees with the tracer).
  Non-critical sites S3, S6, S7, S16-S19, S25-S28, S30, S32, S33, S41-S49, S53, S54 are all value text ('1uH', '5uH', '5uF', '10uH', '50uH', '50uF', '100uF', '5V', '10 A') touching a wire or a symbol; left alone.

FAINT INK / BROKEN STROKES
  The pencil went very light on two long strokes and the skeletoniser fragmented both.
  (a) Rung y~272 between x=692 and x=770. Sampling minimum grey across the rung band shows ink at nearly every column (only 694-698, 738-742 and 766-770 are blank), so it is one stroke. Reconnected with merge [1.1, 0.1]; without it the col-A tap (1.1, 4.0) and the V-AC/I-AC node (0.1, 2.0) would be two separate 2-terminal nets.
  (b) Bottom rail: solid black x=175..486, light and dotted x=487..683, solid again x=684..822. Two separate calls:
      - x=647..692 has ink at essentially every column (only 648-653 and 661-664 blank), the same character as the rest of the rail, so it is connected. Applied with merge [11.1, 12.1], putting the 100uF bottom and the 15V bottom on n7; leaving it broken would strand each of them on a 1-terminal net.
      - x=535..609 contains three genuinely empty gaps of 15, 11 and 20 px (535-549, 560-570, 590-609), by far the weakest ink anywhere on the sheet. Treated as NOT connected, so the bottom rail is two nets (n4 to the left, n7 to the right). This is the one place where the ink alone is arguable and electrical impossibility decides it: joining them would put the 15V source's top node (n4, reached from the y~765 rung through col C down to the bottom rail) and its bottom node on the same net - a short-circuited voltage source. No other break point works: the rail is solid black between col A, col B and col C, and breaking it at x=647..692 instead would leave the 15V bottom alone on its own net. So the break must be between col C and col D, which is exactly where the ink is worst.

REMAINING WARNING (understood, not an error)
  I-DC #8 ends up with both terminals on n4. That is what the sheet draws: col B carries the y~610 rung tap on down to the bottom rail and col C carries the y~765 rung tap down to the same rail, so the 10A source is shunted by the bottom rail. Both column runs are unbroken black ink (column-by-column scan finds no blank row for col B y=620..895 or col C y=770..895), so there is nothing to override. A shunted current source is physically harmless, unlike the shorted voltage source discussed above.

PORT / PIN FIXES
  #4 Capacitor 5uF: the tracer used p2@(147,451) as t0 - that is the 'F' of the '5uF' label touching the lower plate (visible in sites S25-S28). t0 repointed to p1@(174,406), the real top lead; t1 stays p0@(174,451).
  #6 Capacitor 10uF: t0 and t1 both sat on bottom-side ink (p0@(307,514) and p2@(322,514), the latter being the '10u' text). t0 repointed to p1@(301,467) (top lead), t1 to p0.
  #12 Capacitor 100uF: same fault - p0@(622,830) and p2@(632,830) both below the symbol, p2 being the leading stroke of the '100uF' label. t0 repointed to p1@(620,788) (top lead), t1 to p0. Bridge B29, which glued that text stroke onto the bottom lead, was dropped too.
  Every other component already had t0/t1 on the real leads. The unused port candidates on #0 (four, x~845-851) and #1 (p2@(147,187)) are the '3V / 1 kHz' and '1uH' labels; ignored.

CLASSES
  All 13 labels match the drawn symbols: coils for the five inductors, parallel-plate pairs for the five capacitors, circle+sine for V-AC #0, circle+sine+arrow for I-AC #2, circle+arrow for I-DC #8, circle with +/- for V-DC #5 and #11. No class overrides. There is no GND symbol on this sheet, so there is no net '0'.
